dependency_edges.handoff: Functional E/F roles and default scenario parameterize the electron-density profile.
Ne(h) is converted to n(h,f).
The representative E-layer refractive index sets the F-entry angle.
The E-layer exit angle initializes F-layer marching.
The local refractive-index profile drives every F-layer Snell update.
Peak density and height feed the critical-frequency/MUF gate.
The physical feasibility limit should screen candidate carrier frequencies before recursion.
The calm-sea Fresnel coefficient is the baseline multiplied by roughness rho.
The rough-sea amplitude supplies per-reflection loss.
The smooth-ground Fresnel coefficient is reduced by the terrain factor.
The rugged-ground coefficient feeds the matched ground comparison.
D-layer attenuation enters the cumulative SNR ledger.
F-layer range and mirrored descent determine the hop geometry.
Accumulated path distance determines FSPL in the recursive ledger.
Frequency-specific noise initializes SNR0.
Terminal distance, hop count, SNR, and first-hop states feed result tables.
Repeated MHPM paths over a frequency band yield landing-point envelopes.
Each interval length is divided by ship speed.
E/F density and layer-height perturbations modify the refractive state.
Wind perturbations modify the rough-sea energy channel.
Sensitivity outputs qualify the baseline performance conclusions.
